concepts.learning_objective: Classify stakeholders as internal or external users and identify whether their stake is monetary or non-monetary.
Explain the objectives and accounting information requirements of owners, managers, government, prospective owners and banks.
Distinguish capital, revenue and deferred revenue expenditure by the period of benefit and their accounting treatment.
Distinguish capital receipts from revenue receipts with examples.
Analyse how wrong classification of capital and revenue items misstates profit and assets.

topics.title: Financial statements and items of the trading and profit and loss account

concepts.learning_objective: State the objectives and components of the financial statements of a sole proprietor.
Identify which items are debited to the trading account and which to the profit and loss account.
Record closing entries that transfer expenses, revenues and returns to the trading and profit and loss account.

topics.title: Gross profit, net profit and cost of goods sold

concepts.learning_objective: Compute gross profit and net profit and trace how the classification of items affects each.
Compute cost of goods sold using opening stock, purchases, direct expenses and closing stock.
Explain the meaning of operating profit and compute it from net profit.
Identify non-operating expenses and incomes, including abnormal and purely financial items.
Explain the nature of the balance sheet and show capital after adjusting profit and drawings.
Classify balance sheet items as current, fixed, intangible, investments, long-term liabilities or capital.
Arrange assets and liabilities in the order of liquidity or permanence.
Group balance sheet items of similar nature under common headings.
Pass the opening entry that carries balance sheet accounts into the next accounting period.
